findings.claim: HTTP 504 is recorded on the function execution itself, with the CDN also recording 504.
findings.evidence: Each target functionEvents[].httpStatus and proxyEvents[].httpStatus is 504.

findings.claim: The function execution ended at the configured application budget of approximately 28 seconds, well below its 300-second platform limit.
findings.evidence: Function durations are 28006, 28007, 28033, and 28006 ms; configured platform duration is 300 seconds; production partly budget is 28000 ms.

findings.claim: The most strongly supported generation path is application-level abort/timeout handling after the partly audio request exhausts its 28-second budget.
findings.evidence: Production POST catches proxy errors and gatewayError returns 504 for TimeoutError/AbortError without logging; all four end at that budget and have no platform error code or crash.

findings.claim: Platform max-duration timeout, cold start, and function crash do not explain the retrieved metadata.
findings.evidence: Actual duration is ~28s versus max300s, startType=hot, hasFunctionCrashed=false, runtime errorCode empty.

findings.claim: The budget covers obtaining a complete upstream response body and JSON validation as well as retries/backoff.
findings.evidence: retrySpeechRequest wraps request and response.arrayBuffer in withinSpeechBudget; application receives a buffered complete response.

findings.claim: The incoming request time is the proxy timestamp, not a measured completion timestamp.
findings.evidence: For all four, root timestamp equals proxyEvents.timestamp; provider reference defines proxy timestamp as when proxy request was made. Function timeline event follows 19–50ms later.

findings.claim: Three user-agent families classify as chromium and one as CastReader; no complete user agent was retained.
findings.evidence: Fixed-token classification performed in memory from clientUserAgent.

unresolved: No individual exception object/name/stack or response body is retained in these four logs, so TimeoutError versus parent AbortError is not directly observed.

No upstream attempt spans, attempt counts, first-byte timing, body-completion timing, or network failure codes were recovered. The evidence cannot distinguish connect delay, upstream queue/inference delay, stalled body transfer, or retryable responses.

traceId is empty; no request headers exist in the returned schema; the two requestTags contain no recognized correlation key. The application-generated x-request-id is not logged by its timeout catch, so no Vercel-to-upstream or Vercel-to-client event join is proven.
Concurrency 44–45 is provider metadata, not evidence by itself of CPU starvation or overload.
iad1 proves only Vercel function execution region, not full-chain regional compliance.
Derived function end times add the provider duration to the function event timestamp and are explicitly calculations, not separately captured response-completion log entries.

collectionNotes.priorFailureCause: vercel api only accepts API-base paths and rejected the full vercel.com URL before dispatch. This was a tool invocation limitation, not a production error.
collectionNotes.resolvedMethod: Read the exact request-logs endpoint used by installed vercel logs, using the existing CLI credential in memory; persist only sanitized fields.
collectionNotes.traceLookupLimitation: No traceId is available for a direct distributed trace lookup.
